Fix the open animation, add text sizing and idle dismissal

The note used to open by dragging the entire deck across the screen. The panel
resize (56 -> 460 pt) and the state change were landing in the same SwiftUI
pass, so withAnimation interpolated the container's width and the tabs flew in
from mid-screen with it. Video at 30fps put a tab at x=1322pt mid-animation
instead of 1434. The state change now waits two display frames after the resize,
and the duplicate implicit spring on deck.state is gone.

- ⌃+ / ⌃- step the note text size, alongside the Text size menu.
- A fan left untouched collapses after 4s and an idle note after 60s; the watch
  polls the pointer rather than monitoring mouse-moved events globally.

Stop the note appearing from mid-screen; lean the deck; handwritten body

The open animation kept starting from the wrong place. Full-screen video at
30fps showed a tab drawn at x=1029pt — the panel's *leading* edge — for one or
two frames before the note faded in. The panel was being widened as the note
opened, and the NSWindow resize and SwiftUI's relayout land in different frames,
so for one frame the deck laid out against the far edge of an already-wide
panel. Reading the size from the controller instead of a GeometryReader was not
enough; the fix is to stop resizing at all. The fan and the open note now share
one panel width, and "leaving the deck" is tested against the strip by the
screen edge rather than the whole panel.

Also: tabs, chips and the open note each carry a small stable lean derived from
the note id, note bodies are set in Noteworthy (toggleable), and the paper
palette is deeper with a soft gradient.

Add a note font picker, and stop typing jumping after a font change

Changing the size while a note was open made typing jump, and closing and
reopening the note fixed it — the tell that the view's state was stale rather
than the layout being wrong. `tv.font` was updated but `typingAttributes` was
not, so each new character was inserted in the *previous* font and then
rewritten by the restyle pass on the next keystroke. Restyling also rewrote the
whole document without putting the caret back.

- typingAttributes are refreshed whenever the face, size or ink changes.
- The selection is saved and restored across the restyle.
- Note font is now a choice, not a handwriting on/off: a curated list filtered
  to the faces actually installed, so the menu never offers one that would
  silently fall back. Tab labels follow the same face a weight bolder.

Settings window: rebindable shortcuts, Markdown styling, deck controls

Adds a Settings window (⌘, or the pill's menu) where everything applies live.

Shortcuts — all twelve are now rebindable, not just the three global ones. The
recorder has to intercept performKeyEquivalent as well as keyDown, or a
combination matching a menu item is swallowed by the menu before the field sees
it. In-note shortcuts accept a bare key (Close defaults to plain esc) because
they are matched by the open note itself; the global ones still refuse a
modifier-less combination, which would swallow that key system-wide. Key names
come from the live keyboard layout via UCKeyTranslate.

Markdown — headings, emphasis, code, strikethrough, quotes and bullets style
themselves as you type, and the syntax is hidden rather than dimmed. Hiding
characters without deleting them means marking their glyphs .null in a
NSLayoutManager subclass; colouring them clear leaves their width behind and the
caret still walks through them. That in turn means building an explicit TextKit
1 stack, since a plain NSTextView gets TextKit 2 where NSLayoutManager is never
consulted. Markers reappear on the caret's line so they stay editable, and the
stored text is untouched either way.

Also: ⇧⌘A archives the note in front of you — ⌥⌘L only ever opened the archive
window. Detection area is configurable, and a tab can be press-held and dragged
to reorder the deck.

Release 1.0.8: update appcast

Settings cog, hover-to-open, smoother tab drag, fixed note sizes

Reordering tabs by dragging was inconsistent and flashed. Three separate causes:
the drop target was recomputed from the live offset, so jitter at a slot
boundary flipped it every frame; the spring keyed to that target also covered
the tab under the pointer, so it lagged rather than tracked; and the drag offset
lived on the column, re-rendering six tabs with shadows and materials sixty
times a second. The target now needs 60% of a slot before it moves, the dragged
tab carries its own un-animated offset, and the column only hears about slot
changes. The idle watch also no longer collapses the deck mid-drag, which was
yanking it shut whenever the pointer strayed out of the edge strip.

Dragging the note's corner to resize is gone. It drove an NSWindow resize, a
SwiftUI relayout and a TextKit reflow from one continuous gesture, and each fix
surfaced another failure — the worst being a full text-storage restyle per
frame, because updateNSView compared a freshly built NSColor that never matched.
Note size is now four fixed choices in Settings, and a previously dragged size
carries over to the nearest one. Restyling is gated on a cheap token regardless,
so it no longer runs on unrelated re-renders.

Also: a settings cog under the plus, hovering a tab can open its note (off by
default), shortcuts laid out in two columns, and export surfaced in All Notes.

Let the deck stay fanned out instead of folding back to the pill

The tabs and their labels only exist while the pointer is on the edge,
so a deck you want to read at a glance has to be hovered first. This
adds a preference that keeps them there.

Only the deck's *resting* state changes: notes open, close and idle away
exactly as before. The idle poll now runs above the resting state rather
than above .rest, so it still tidies an open note but no longer chases a
fan that is meant to stay put.

Toggling the preference off while the pointer is on the deck restarts
that poll rather than pulling the tabs away mid-hover.

Add a deck size preference so the tabs can be scaled

Every deck metric was a fixed constant, so the tabs were whatever size
they were — too small to read comfortably on a dense display, too large
on a small one.

All of them now pass through one multiplier: tab width, the lap between
tabs, the label type, the chips, the plus button and the resting pill,
so the deck scales as a whole rather than drifting out of proportion.
Layout already sizes each tab's visible strip from the *measured* label,
so scaling the type carries the pitch with it for free.

The System face has no bold cut and so always lands on the fallback
font — that path scales too, or "System" would be the one face that
quietly ignored the setting.

Merge PR #2: superseded by PR #8's IME handling

PR #2 adds two guards: do not assign tv.string while the input method
owns a marked-text range, and do not restyle during composition. PR #8's
coordinator already guards hasMarkedText() at every one of those points —
synchronize, textDidChange, textViewDidChangeSelection, applyIncremental
and applyFullPassIfSafe — and additionally sets needsFullPass so the note
is styled once the composition commits, which #2 does not.

Resolved to the merged tree with no change. Behaviour still needs a real
IME to confirm; this only records that the code paths are covered.

Take PR #5's CI hardening, without the rest of the branch

From PR #5, verified independently before taking:
- Nothing from the event object is interpolated into a shell any more. A
  workflow_dispatch version input is attacker-controlled text and ${{ }}
  pastes it into the script; it now arrives as an env var and has to be
  numeric SemVer.
- actions/* pinned to immutable SHAs. Each SHA was checked against the
  tag it claims through the GitHub API — the two in the PR are genuine.
- Sparkle's tarball is checksummed before extraction. The expected digest
  in the PR matches the real 2.9.6 release, downloaded and hashed here.
- permissions: contents: read on the build workflow.

Deliberately not taken:
- The PR replaced main's rebase-and-retry appcast push with a plain git
  push, undoing the fix for the race that shipped 1.1.0 without a feed.
  The hardening is applied on top of the retry loop instead.
- It deleted pages.yml outright. Kept and pinned the same way.
- It dropped fetch-sparkle.sh's cache short-circuit, so every local build
  re-downloaded Sparkle. Kept, with the checksum applied to the pinned
  version only.

Reconcile the merged features with each other

Three things only show up once the branches sit together:

- #6 and #10 cancelled out. "Keep the deck open" makes the fan the resting
  state, so the pill is never on screen, and ⌥-drag required state == .rest.
  It now asks for the resting state, whichever that is.
- #10 pinned displayTarget to the dragged screen on every drag, including
  under the default "All Displays" — nudging the pill would silently take
  the deck off every other monitor. It now only follows the drag when the
  deck is already pinned to one display.
- #10's drag runs a nested modal loop on the main thread waiting on
  .distantFuture. If the mouse-up is ever delivered elsewhere the app
  wedges with no way out; it now polls and checks the button state.

Remove the bloat the merged branches brought with them

- docs/superpowers/specs/… (#8) is agent scaffolding, not project docs.
  The rationale it carries is in the merge commit and the code comments.
- Dead code the sweep in #5 was right about, re-checked here: paperShade,
  Updater.canCheck (both branches), DeckGeom.tabHeightMax/tabHeightMin/
  plusInset, and the unused Combine and AppKit imports.

Kept from #8: Tests/EditorStyleEngineTests.swift and scripts/test-editor.sh
— they build and pass, and they are the only automated check in the repo.

Release build and the editor tests both pass.
Document the deck size and keep-open preferences

Markdown links in notes

[label](url) joins the other inline styles: the label is underlined and
carries the destination, the brackets and the URL hide off the caret line
like every other marker. ⌘-click opens it; a plain click still places the
caret.

Only http, https and mailto are ever given the .link attribute, checked
again at the click before anything reaches NSWorkspace. Notes can be
imported, and a note is not a place a javascript: or file: URL should
become one gesture away from running.

Two things the tests caught:
- The markdown fast-path character set had no '[', so the whole pass was
  skipped for a line whose only Markdown was a link.
- .link and .underlineStyle had to join the reset list. Styling is
  line-scoped, so nothing comes back to a line later to tidy up, and
  deleting the brackets would have left the text underlined and live.

Merging dev into main is the release button

dev is the integration branch and main is the release branch, so the
release job now triggers on a push to main rather than on a tag.

- The version comes from "release: X.Y.Z" in the merge commit message,
  and otherwise bumps the patch — a hotfix should not need ceremony. A
  version that is already tagged is a no-op, so a re-run is safe.
- scripts/make-release-notes.sh writes the changelog from the pull
  requests the release contains, each with a link and its author. It
  emits markdown for the release page and HTML for the Sparkle dialog.
  Membership is decided by whether a PR's merge commit is reachable from
  HEAD but not from the previous tag — filtering by merge date looks
  equivalent and is not, because work merged into dev sits unreleased
  until dev lands, so a date window gives it to whichever release comes
  next even when that one does not contain it.
- concurrency: two merges landing together would otherwise compute the
  same version and race for the same tag.
- gh release create --target pins the tag to the commit the job built.
- Docs, site, media and appcast paths are excluded, so a README push to
  main never cuts a release. One push block cannot filter paths for
  branches without filtering them for tags too, so the tag trigger is
  gone; workflow_dispatch replaces it and needs no tag pushed first.
- build.yml now also builds dev.

Dry-run against v1.1.0..dev lists all five merged PRs with their authors.

Credit work that shipped without its own pull request

A "Thanks-to: @handle — what for" trailer on the commit that takes the
work puts it in the release notes, on the page and in the Sparkle dialog.
The credit then lives with the change instead of in a file someone has to
remember to clear before the next release. Co-Authored-By counts too, but
only when it resolves to a real GitHub account — tool and bot trailers
have no profile to link to.

Stop reading UserDefaults on every geometry access

The deck-size merge routed every DeckGeom metric through
Settings.deckScale, which is a UserDefaults read — a lock and a
dictionary lookup, measured at ~320 ns. SwiftUI reads those metrics
dozens of times per body evaluation, so every frame of the fan animation
and every frame of a tab drag paid it dozens of times over.

deckScale, deckYRatio and noteSizeIndex are now memoized in Settings.
Every write already funnels through their setters and everything runs on
the main thread, so the cache cannot go stale. 800k reads through the
real DeckGeom: 215.9 ms before, 6.7 ms after, identical results.

Checked while in there, with `leaks` against a copy that had been running
71 minutes: zero leaks, 0 bytes. Monitors and the idle timer are removed
in deinit, the deck views hold their controller weak/unowned, the editor
bridge holds its text view weak, and dismantleNSView clears the TextKit
delegates — nothing needed fixing.

Release 1.2.0: update appcast

Keep the pill in place while the panel grows into the fan

Hovering the pill flashed it at the top corner of the screen before the
tabs fanned out (#11). `layout(for:)` resizes the panel with
`setFrame(display: true)`, and AppKit lays the existing SwiftUI tree out
at the new full-screen height *before* SwiftUI re-evaluates the body. The
body read its height from `DeckModel.panelHeight`, which for that one
frame still held the pill height, so the pill's top padding was zero and
the `.topTrailing` ZStack put it in the corner — where the opacity
transition then faded it out. The same thing happened in reverse when the
panel shrank back after a collapse.

Take the height from a GeometryReader in the layout pass instead of the
cached value, and place the pill from `deckYRatio` so it resolves to the
same screen position at any panel height: zero padding in the resting
panel, and exactly where the resting panel sits in the full-height one.
The `panelHeight` mirror has no readers left and goes.

Verified with `NOTY_DEBUG_DECK=1` probes in the layout pass: the stale
pass now reports pillTop=513 at 1073 high and the shrink pass pillTop=0
at 47 high — the same screen spot both ways.

Quick capture and the noty:// URL scheme

⇧⌘Space (rebindable, alongside the other global shortcuts) pops a small
floating box on whichever screen the pointer is on: type, hit return, and
the text becomes a note in the deck — no editor, no focus ceremony. The

settings open their windows. URL text only ever becomes note content;
anything unrecognised is ignored.

Quick capture no longer activates the app

NSApp.activate() stole focus from whatever was in front — its window
dimmed, focus rings dropped, and everything snapped back on dismiss,
which read as UI flashing behind the box. A non-activating panel can
take key input while the front app stays active (the Spotlight pattern),
so the activate/deactivate pair is gone and the content is laid out
before the panel is ordered front.

Verified with an injected keystroke: the character lands in the box while
the front app keeps the menu bar and its focus.

One hot-key press is one toggle, however long it is held

Carbon delivers a fresh kEventHotKeyPressed for every keyboard autorepeat
while the combo is held, and a toggle per event flapped the capture box
open and shut. Toggles inside the repeat window now count as the same
press, and a resign-key in that window re-asserts key instead of
dismissing — key status can bounce while the app in front is still
processing the hot-key's own release.

Reproduced and verified by injecting the hot-key with HID autorepeat
events: before, six deliveries left the box flapping; after, a held combo
opens it once and a second press closes it.

Arm the hot-key repeat window on close as well as open

The debounce stamped its clock only in show(), so holding the combo to
close dismissed on the first event and reopened on its first autorepeat
— the same flap in the other direction. Any accepted toggle now starts
the window, and repeats inside it are swallowed regardless of which way
the box was going.

Merge PR #24: universal Intel + Apple Silicon binaries

Taken with three adjustments:
- Debug builds compile one native slice; universal matters for what ships,
  and doubling every local edit loop pays for a slice nobody runs.
- The test binary likewise: tests only run on the machine that built them.
- The Finder layout AppleScript can no longer fail the release. It is the
  flakiest thing in the DMG script and entirely cosmetic, so a failure
  logs and moves on instead of costing the release its disk image.

Conflict with #23 in test-editor.sh resolved by keeping the localisation
test in the compile and dropping the universal loop there.

Ship one DMG per architecture instead of a universal image

A universal binary cost every download a third more (1.85 MB → 2.47 MB
measured) for a slice each Mac ignores. Releases now build twice and ship
Noty.dmg (Apple Silicon, the original name so every existing install and
link keeps working) and Noty-intel.dmg.

Sparkle knows one feed, so the split means two: appcast.xml keeps serving
Apple Silicon — every install to date is arm64 — and the x86_64 build has
appcast-intel.xml baked into its SUFeedURL, so Intel updates stay Intel.
Both are generated and signed by the release job and pushed together.

Local release builds stay universal (BUILD_ARCHS overrides), debug builds
stay native-only, and the site's download button gains an Intel companion.

Verified locally end to end: both builds carry the right SUFeedURL, both
DMGs package, both appcasts sign against the real key and validate.

Add an option to hide the deck completely at rest

Closes #19

Nothing shows until the pointer reaches the edge — no pill, no dashes.
The invisible detection strip still wakes the tabs, so the notes stay one
hover away; they just leave the screen alone until asked for. Off by
default, localised in both catalogues.

Pull a note off the deck and leave it anywhere on the screen

Implements #21 (the first idea)

Grab the open note by its tab-gutter and drag past the threshold: a
floating panel takes over under the cursor at the note's own on-screen
position, the in-deck sheet hides — it must stay in the hierarchy, since
removing it would end the very gesture steering the detach — and the deck
steps back to the fan on release.

The floating note keeps the deck's manners: the same editor, autosave,
Markdown, text direction; Esc or a minute of idle tucks it home to the
edge with a slide, unless it is pinned. One floats at a time, matching
the deck's one-open-note model, and expanding a note that is already
floating focuses it instead of opening the same body twice. Deleting or
archiving it elsewhere takes the panel with it.

The release notes script also gains an Answered-issues section, built
from Closes/Fixes/Implements #N in commit messages, so a request that
lands as a direct commit still credits the person who asked.

Resize the floating note from any edge or corner

.resizable on the borderless panel turns every edge into a native
live-resize band — system cursors, system smoothness, none of the
hand-rolled corner-drag that made the old in-deck resize glitch. The
incremental styler means a resize triggers no restyle at all.

The note keeps whatever size you stretch it to (saved at the end of the
live resize, not per frame) and comes off the deck at that size next
time. Resizing counts as activity, so a note cannot tuck away mid-grab.
Floor of 280×220 so it cannot be squeezed into an unusable sliver.

Dragging the floating note no longer presses the button it grabbed

The drag gesture covered the whole header, buttons included, and
WindowDragGesture moves the window under the cursor — so the release
always landed inside the very button the grab started on. Dragging by
the pin pinned the note; dragging by the close button would have closed
it. Only the title strip drags now.

Revert "Dragging the floating note no longer presses the button it grabbed"

This reverts commit 80e163acec28218e19e357c7c49934f0d19d867a.

The pin decides whether the floating note stays on top

The panel was hard-coded to .floating, riding above every window forever.
Unpinned it is now an ordinary window — covered when you work elsewhere,
raised when clicked, tucked when idle. Pinned it stays above everything
and never tucks, which is what a pin on a sticky means. The pull itself
keeps .floating so the note cannot slide under the deck panel mid-drag,
and a pin toggled from All Notes takes effect within a tick.

Clicking a floating note's tab lifts it above the active app

The tab click already routed to the floating panel instead of opening a
second editor, but an unpinned note sits at normal level and Noty is an
accessory app — makeKeyAndOrderFront fronts it among Noty's own windows
only, which is nowhere when it is buried under the app being used.
orderFrontRegardless does the actual lifting.

Lift the floating note at floating level, settle back per the pin

Front-of-level ordering for a background app's normal-level window is
the flaky corner of AppKit; raising at .floating first makes the lift
unambiguous, then the pin decides where the note settles. A couple of
NSLog lines stay on the path so a report of a missed lift can be read
straight from the unified log.

Fix hotkey note creation, and titles rendering white in dark mode

Fixes #27

Two things went wrong when a global shortcut created a note:
- The staged expand choreography (resize, two-frame delay, animated state
  flip) assumes a settled, watched panel. Fired with the pointer nowhere
  near the deck it stalled mid-flight, leaving the note stuck invisible
  at its transition's start with just its tab poking through the edge.
  A hotkey expand from rest now shows the note outright, no transition.
- .fullScreenAuxiliary was granted unconditionally, so the deck joined
  full-screen spaces even with "Show over full-screen apps" off — the
  setting only ever changed the window level. The flag is now gated too.

Separately, note titles rendered white on the paper in dark mode: a
plain-style field draws its placeholder in the system secondary label
colour and ignores every modifier put on the prompt — and a derived
title always shows *as* the placeholder. The placeholder is now our own
Text overlay, which styles like anything else.

All three verified by injected hotkey and screenshot, before and after.

Quick capture can append to an existing note

Closes #26

A row of chips under the capture box picks the destination: a fresh note
(the default, unchanged behaviour), or any of the first eight tabs — the
captured text is appended to the end of that note's body. ⌘1 keeps a
fresh note, ⌘2… aim at a tab, and the box's paper colour follows the
choice so it previews where the text will land. A target deleted while
the box sat open falls back to creating a new note.

Capture destinations as dots in the header, top right

The chip row read as clutter. Destinations are now small colour dots in
the header's right corner — the deck's own vocabulary — with a ringed
plus for a fresh note, a ring marking the choice, a tooltip naming each,
and the header label switching to the chosen note's title so one glance
answers where the text will land. Box back to its original height.

fix: convert every markdown task line, not only the first

String.replacingOccurrences(options: .regularExpression) cannot request
.anchorsMatchLines, so ^ matched only the start of the whole string and a
document with several tasks converted just the first one. toMarkdown was not
anchored at all, so a marker used mid-sentence became list syntax.

Both now go through NSRegularExpression with .anchorsMatchLines, and use
[ \t] rather than \s so a match cannot swallow a newline.

feat: sync notes to iPhone and iPad through the iCloud Drive folder

Each note becomes one Markdown file in
~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/Noty/, with a front-matter
header carrying its identity, colour, dates and order. Edits travel both ways,
files written on a phone are adopted as notes, and deletions propagate.

This is the iCloud Drive folder, not CloudKit: CKContainer needs the
com.apple.developer.icloud-container-identifiers entitlement, which needs a
provisioning profile, Xcode and a paid developer account. The folder is a plain
path a non-sandboxed app may use, and the system daemon syncs it.

Off by default. Synced files are plaintext — they have to be readable on the
phone — while the local database stays AES-GCM encrypted.

SyncPlan.actions is a pure function of (notes, folder, last-sync index), so the
decision table is unit-tested; CloudSync reaches the world through two
protocols, so the runner is tested against in-memory fakes. Deletion follows
only from a document confirmed absent: an unreadable file, a failed read or an
evicted .icloud placeholder never delete a note.
docs: iCloud Drive sync, what to use on the phone, and the privacy trade-off

feat: inline images in note bodies

Paste, drop, or pick images into a note; they render inline between
lines of text and mix freely with it. Images live as files under
Application Support (referenced by a hidden ![image](noty-img://id)
token), keeping the encrypted SQLite store small and letting one image
be shared across notes.

- Resize via a hover handle; the width rides inside the token, so it
  survives restarts and export/import (archive v3)
- The token stays hidden at all times; pressing delete at an image
  first reveals the raw token selected, and only a second delete
  removes it — space/return/click elsewhere restores the image
- Arrow keys treat an image like a single character, caret can sit on
  either side
- Deleting a note cleans up its unreferenced images; orphaned files
  are swept at launch
- Previews and derived titles strip tokens so paths never leak

refactor: throwing persistence with debounced saves and honest error surface

Store gains a throwing API (load/upsert/delete) over an injectable
dbURL/keyURL pair; Crypto becomes an instance that never mints a new key
over an existing database and installs fresh keys atomically (O_EXCL +
fsync + link). NoteStore owns all save debouncing — per-view autosave
timers are gone; failed writes stay in unsavedIDs, are surfaced once via
NSAlert, retried on flush, and block quit until they land. Exports flush
first, reserve filenames exclusively, and archives (v3) carry the pinned
flag while imports validate colors.

The per-launch derived-title migration is removed deliberately: it also
wiped any title a user typed that happened to equal the first body line,
on every launch. PersistenceTests pins the new behavior; the one-time
cost is a frozen derived title for direct upgrades from <=1.5.x, which
self-heals when the title is edited.
